Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

offer verb and noun

hold out, present

also hold out, proffer, an offer

classical

Publil. Sent. B 1: ultrō sī offerās
Vulg. Lc. 24.42: obtulērunt eī partem piscis assī

offerō, offerre, obtulī, oblātum

verb, irregular (ob + ferō), conjugation

offer, hold out, present

ultrō offerre, to offer unasked; sē offerre, to present oneself or put oneself forward.

Other words

  • dēferō, dēferre, dētulī, dēlātum — offer (a post, an honour, a task) to someone

    verb, irregular (dē + ferō), conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BG 2.4.7: ad hunc … summam tōtīus bellī omnium voluntāte dēferrī

  • condiciō, condiciōnis f. — an offer, terms proposed

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.42.2: nōn respuit condiciōnem Caesar; M-O s.v. deal, terms (of agreement), settlement offer

    alicui condiciōnem ferre, to make someone an offer (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Bis est grātum quod opus est, ultrō sī offerās.

    What is needed is twice as welcome if you offer it unasked.Publil. Sent. B 1

  • Habētis hīc aliquid quod mandūcētur? At illī obtulērunt eī partem piscis assī et favum mellis.

    Have you anything here to eat? And they offered him a piece of grilled fish and a honeycomb.Vulg. Lc. 24.41–42

  • Nōn respuit condiciōnem Caesar jamque eum ad sānitātem revertī arbitrābātur, cum id quod anteā petentī dēnegāsset ultrō pollicērētur.

    Caesar did not reject the offer, and thought the man was coming to his senses, since he was now offering of his own accord what he had refused when asked.Caes. BG 1.42.2

See also offer, give, gift, bargain.
